activities.caption: file each decision under the half of the craft it belongs to
activities.name: typoCraftSort

config.prompt: File each decision under the half of the craft it belongs to:

items.label: serif or sans for the body
a modular scale of 1.25 for headings

config.why: The choice is perhaps a tenth of the craft; the spacing decisions — measure, leading, hierarchy, space — decide whether the chosen face can work at all.

activities.anchor: the measurements that decide everything practical
activities.caption: pair each anatomical term with what it decides
activities.name: typoAnatomyMatch

config.prompt: Pair each anatomical term with what it decides:

pairs.right: the lowercase body the eye actually reads — two '16 px' faces can differ a size class
the opening of a c or e — tight ones close up and blur at small sizes
thick versus thin within one letter — high reads refined, fragile on low-resolution screens
the enclosed spaces that keep letters alive at heavy weights

config.why: Anatomy is not trivia — each measurement predicts how the face survives small sizes, heavy weights and screens.

activities.anchor: Typefaces sort into families with personalities earned historically
activities.caption: rebuild the serif timeline — oldest first
activities.name: typoSerifOrder

config.prompt: Rebuild the serif timeline — oldest first:
items: Old-style — Garamond, 16th century: humanist, angled stress, calligraphy's memory
Didone — Bodoni and Didot: extreme contrast, Enlightenment geometry
Slab — mechanical serifs: the poster voice
config.why: The sub-families trace five centuries of taste, from the scribal hand to industrial poster print — each age correcting the last.

activities.anchor: Comfortable reading is engineered with four variables
activities.caption: call the width of the canonical measure
activities.name: typoMeasureEst

config.prompt: Body text set at the canonical 66 characters, averaging ≈8 px per character at 16 px — how wide is the measure?
config.why: 66 × 8 ≈ 528 px — about 33 em at 16 px, which is why a max-width: 33em container is the web's most quietly correct line of CSS.
config.context: 33em reproduces the same measure at any font size

activities.anchor: the visual ranking that lets a reader's eye land where importance lives
activities.caption: run the squint test — and fix what it shows
activities.name: typoSquintBranch

config.root: Squint test: your page dissolves into uniform grey mud.

start.text: Nothing stands out: title, headings and body all read as the same density.

choices.label: Reach for a bigger heading font
choices.feedback: Size is only the second lever — a bigger title in the same mud still reads as one slab.

choices.label: Add space: group related blocks, separate the groups
choices.feedback: Separation does more than any font size; the pattern of light and dark begins to appear.

choices.label: Add a third accent colour to key phrases
choices.feedback: The undergraduate's third colour — decoration added to a page that has no ranking yet.

sizeTrap.text: Two sizes, same density — the squint still shows mud.

choices.label: Regroup with space instead
choices.feedback: Grouping and separation is the lever the mud was missing.

colourTrap.text: Now the page is mud with confetti.

choices.label: Take the colour out and regroup with space
choices.feedback: Colour can rank later; it cannot create the grouping the page lacks.

spaceFix.text: Groups breathe apart; the scanning path — title, heads, body, captions — now survives the squint.

config.why: Space is hierarchy's most underused lever; the squint test judges the pattern of density, not the fonts.

activities.anchor: The craft layer that separates designed from assembled lives at pair-level scale
activities.caption: find the backwards claim — the micro-craft rules
activities.name: typoMicroSpot

config.prompt: One of these micro-typographic claims is backwards — click it:
lines: Kerning adjusts a specific pair — AV, To, ry.
All-caps text set at normal tracking looks airy and needs no help.
Ligatures such as fi prevent collisions — two letters, one drawing.
config.correction: All-caps set at normal tracking looks cramped — uniform heights leave the eye no rhythm, so capitals always need extra tracking.
config.why: The standing rule: uniform-height capitals starve the eye of rhythm, which is why all-caps always takes extra tracking.

activities.anchor: a serif body with a sans headline
activities.caption: two ways to pair — drag the divider
activities.name: typoPairCompare

config.prompt: Two ways to pair — drag the divider:

before.label: contrast by family
before.text: serif body, sans headline — two voices, each arguing its post

after.label: one superfamily
after.text: a single family at several weights — hierarchy by weight, one voice throughout

config.why: Both are correct; what fails is similarity — two humanist serifs blur into a mistake.

activities.caption: file each setting under its figures
activities.name: typoFiguresSort

config.prompt: File each setting under its figures:

items.label: a column of prices in a table
old print where 3, 4, 7 and 9 dance along the baseline

config.why: Lining for tables and UI, where columns must align; old-style for running text — the book designer's default and the reason old print feels alive.

activities.anchor: adds its own layer of the craft, because
activities.caption: fill the blanks — the interface numbers
activities.name: typoUICloze

config.text: Interface rhythm is spacing arithmetic: line-height %%0%%–1.6 for body, tighter for headings; labels align to their inputs; and numerals are %%1%%-aligned so magnitudes compare. Accessibility turns the numbers contractual: minimum %%2%%, and the layout must survive zooming to %%3%%%.
config.hint: The body line-height band starts just under one and a half; numerals align on the magnitude side; zoom-tolerance is double.
